nodes.bodyText:
🐛 Bug
Properties defined in classes that inherit from torch.nn.Module raise a misleading error message if non-existent properties are used inside the property definition. The error message reports the incorrect property as missing.
To Reproduce
Run the following code snippet:
import torch.nn as nn

class CustomModule(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__()
    
    @property
    def property_a(self):
        return self.property_b

m = CustomModule()
print(m.property_a)
Expected behavior
Running the code snippet results in the following error message:
AttributeError: 'CustomModule' object has no attribute 'property_a'

This is misleading because the missing attribute is actually property_b. If the same code is implemented in a class that doesn't inherit from torch.nn.Module, the resulting error message is more appropriate since it reports property_b as missing. For example:
class CustomModule2:
    def __init__(self):
        pass

    @property
    def property_a(self):
        return self.property_b

m2 = CustomModule2()
print(m2.property_a)
Displays the following error message:
AttributeError: 'CustomModule2' object has no attribute 'property_b'

This is a followup to #13049, where I discovered that one big aten overhead is calling DeviceGuard a lot. I've been removing unnecessary DeviceGuard calls, but reached a point where it is not obvious what can be removed. In this issue I investigate exactly where DeviceGuard is being called to come up with potential solutions to improve the overhead.
Some numbers

benchmarking DeviceGuard with gbenchmark: ~200ns per DeviceGuard. Some DeviceGuards don't actually cost anything, but let's ignore those for now.

DeviceGuard callsites for aten LSTM forward pass + backward pass full data
DeviceGuard callsites for JIT LSTM forward pass + backward pass full data
Analysis
Since these are all running on the same device, we don't need all the DeviceGuard calls in theory.
There used to be around 3x as many DeviceGuard calls for JIT LSTM. However, since the overhead is only 2.5% of the runtime now, one solution is to just do nothing about the DeviceGuard calls and leave them as-is.

To Reproduce

Run the code below in runtime

class TestView(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self):
        super(TestView, self).__init__()
        self.conv2d = nn.Conv2d(22, 32, kernel_size=1, bias=True)
        self.fc = nn.Linear(15488, 3)

    def forward(self, x):
        x = self.conv2d(x)
        
        print(type(x.size()[0]))

        x = x.view([x.size(0), -1])
        x = self.fc(x)
        return x

🐛 Bug
Repeatedly calling torch.inverse() makes memory leakage, which gets severer when the computation graph is complex.
To Reproduce
Minimum working example below; the reported memory usage increases linearly.
import torch
from resource import *


S = 256
X = torch.randn(S, S, requires_grad=True)

for i in range(10000):
    if i % 100 == 0:
        print(i, '\t', getrusage(RUSAGE_SELF).ru_maxrss, 'kB used')

    Z = X.sum(1, True) + torch.linspace(-S, S, S)
    Y = X * torch.erf(Z).sum(1, True)
    loss = Y.t().mm(Y).inverse().sum() + Y.sum()
    loss.backward()
Below is the output; exact number might differ each run, but the memory usage always increases linearly. This will eventually hog all of available memory and cause problems in long training runs.
0 	 139564 kB used
100 	 157264 kB used
200 	 157988 kB used
300 	 158888 kB used
400 	 159676 kB used
500 	 160392 kB used
600 	 161788 kB used
700 	 162140 kB used
800 	 162892 kB used
900 	 163800 kB used
1000 	 164964 kB used
...

(Calling backward() is just for demonstration purposes, and the problem persists with no autograd at all)
Expected behavior
The memory usage should stay constant at a certain level.
Environment
(CUDA info below should be irrelevant since I'm only using CPU tensors in the example above)

nodes.bodyText:
🚀 Feature
Taking a current look at the JIT optimization framework there are a couple of feature missing.
We do not have a structure that captures post pass analysis of the optimization pass. Analysis are fundamental in optimization as they allow us to understand the necessary passes better. For example if PyTorch had a simple analysis per pass that calculated the number of nodes in the computational graph changed we could introduce features such as fixed point optimization. We could mature even further to Immutable passes (analysis passes) which outline in what order to apply passes to maximize performance. Currently we have a very trivial implementation of optimization which simply runs passes in linear order.
Another feature are pass managers. PyTorch implicitly does this by defining families of optimization passes (e.g. PeepholeOptimizeImpl implements a family of peephole optimization). An explicit OO implementation of pass managers will substantially clean up the code.
Simplifying the implementation of passes will increase agility. There's a lot of code reuse happening with respect to iterating the graph and checking for a pattern to apply a transform. If we could implement type's of passes (e.g. PredicatePass/PatternMatchPass, LoopPass), we could simplify code and reduce code reuse.
Motivation
I'm hoping by introducing these concepts to PyTorch's JIT we could mature the optimization framework and increase the performance of PyTorch in general.
Pitch
This same approach and features I've implemented in the ONNX optimization framework. If we agree that PyTorch needs these features I can start working on this.
nodes.title: Maturing JIT Optimization Framework

nodes.bodyText:
Hi,
I'm considering to implement SSD models inference (but not training) in Caffe2. The models are trained either in TF OD API or in Caffe SSD branch. In both cases, they do essentially the same, with some minor implementation differences. I was able to port models directly from TF OD API to Caffe SSD with identical results, so they do the same.
As far as I know, at the moment, there is no DetectionOutput layer (with class agnostic nms) equivalent. Also, Mask R-CNN's use im_info and input FM height and width to figure out, how to tile anchors, which are implemented as separate blob. So there is no PriorBox layer as well, which performs tiling.
There seem to be three solutions here: 1) modify BoxWithNMSLimit/GenerateProposals and related stuff, 2) write separate PriorBoxOp and DetectionOutputOp; 3) don't change anything in Caffe2: just write separate utility code that implements detection output (priorboxes are tiled just in this code based on input size). In this case the code runs over concats of bbox deltas and confidences after the network is finished.
Is there any interest in such contribution? How is it better for you to implement those if there is interest?
In any case, at the moment I'm interested in porting Caffe2 with max existing fucntionality to Windows, so this is a question on possible future continuation of Caffe2 usage.

Run the following snippet.

        [ 3.8404,  3.9303,  1.0525, -1.9818],

        [0., 0., 0., 0.]])

CUDA seems to work well in this case, maybe because the matrix is small, but you can make it fail too:
import torch
torch.random.manual_seed(1)
N=5000
b = torch.randn([N, N], device='cuda')
print(torch.any(torch.isnan(b @ b.t())))

We would expect the two matrices to have the same result. In the second one, we would not expect a NaN to appear after a Matrix multiplication.

torch.sum closes all pipes of processes which aren't even interacting with pytorch at all. Error appears on Windows 10 with pytorch version 0.4.1. Not reproducible on Linux.
To Reproduce
import torch
from torch.multiprocessing import Process, Queue, Lock, Pipe

def create_list(length, queue, lock, pipe):
    out = []
    while True:
        pipe.recv()
        for i in range(length):
            out.append(i)
        with lock:
            queue.put(out)

def main():
    queue = Queue()
    lock = Lock()
    pipe = Pipe()

    process = Process(target=create_list, args=(10, queue, lock, pipe[1]), daemon=True)
    process.start()

    pipe = pipe[0]

    pipe.send(True)
    while queue.empty():
        pass
    while not queue.empty():
        with lock:
            out = queue.get()
        tensor = torch.tensor(out)
        tensor = torch.sum(tensor)
        # tensor = torch.prod(tensor)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

Expected behavior

🐛 Bug
A possible CPU-side memory leak even when fitting on the GPU using PyTorch 0.4.1.
To Reproduce
I am quite new to PyTorch, having used TF/Keras extensively in the past, but am now trying to use PyTorch as a replacement. I decided to start small with a seq2seq Skip-Thought model, cobbled together using the PyTorch NLP tutorials. Everything seems to work fine when I run small scale tests, however, when I use the code to run a large scale fit on 3000 separate paragraphs (each paragraph having a variable number of sentences) I notice that my system RAM usage slowly goes up as the script runs, until eventually it hits 100% and the box becomes unresponsive and has to be force rebooted. The Linux box has 64 GB of RAM, and when the script starts, usage is 4.7% but this climbs steadily over time to 100%, at which point the box becomes unresponsive.
Since I'm new to PyTorch, I'm not sure if perhaps I'm doing something blatantly wrong in my code which would account for this behaviour?
This is my core fitting logic, which runs as a script on linux:
device = 'cuda'
model = SkipThought(len(text_dictionary.token2id), 128, 256, nn.NLLLoss()).to(device)

// corpus_orig is a list of lists where each list-element is a text paragraph with multiple sentences
n_iters=len(corpus_orig)

start = time.time()
print_loss_total = 0

optimizer = optim.SGD(model.parameters(), lr=0.01)

for xi in range(1, n_iters + 1):
    x = corpus_orig[xi - 1]
    sents = [x for x in map(str.strip, x.split('. ')) if len(x) > 0]
    for i in range(1, len(sents) - 1):
        input_tensor, prev_tensor, next_tensor = tensorsFromPair( (sents[i], sents[i - 1], sents[i + 1]) )

        optimizer.zero_grad()
        
        loss, prev_output, next_output = model(input_tensor, prev_tensor, next_tensor, use_teacher_forcing=True)
        
        loss.backward(retain_graph=True)    // pytorch says I need retain_graph=True, otherwise I get an error here
        optimizer.step()
        
        print_loss_total += loss.item()

    print_loss_avg = print_loss_total
    print_loss_total = 0
    print('%s (%d %d%%) %.4f' % (timeSince(start, xi / n_iters),
                         xi, xi / n_iters * 100, print_loss_avg), flush=True)

Here are the helper functions which create the tensors passed to the model by converting all text words into indices from a predefined gensim dictionary:
def indexesFromSentence(sentence):
    return text_dictionary.doc2idx(sentence.split())

def tensorFromSentence(sentence):
    indexes = indexesFromSentence(sentence)
    indexes.append(EOS_token)
    return torch.tensor(indexes, dtype=torch.long, device=device).view(-1, 1)

def tensorsFromPair(pair):
    input_tensor = tensorFromSentence(pair[0])
    prev_tensor = tensorFromSentence(pair[1])
    next_tensor = tensorFromSentence(pair[2])
    return (input_tensor, prev_tensor, next_tensor)

And, finally, here is the SkipThought model itself, with all its helper classes (apologies for the wall of code):
class EncoderRNN(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, vocab_size, embedding_size, gru_size):
        super(EncoderRNN, self).__init__()
        self.vocab_size = vocab_size
        self.embedding_size = embedding_size
        self.gru_size = gru_size

        self.embedding = nn.Embedding(vocab_size, embedding_size)
        self.gru = nn.GRU(embedding_size, gru_size)

    def forward(self, sentence, hidden):
        embeddings = self.embedding(sentence)
        embeddings = F.tanh(embeddings)
        output, hidden = self.gru(embeddings, hidden)
        
        return output, hidden

    def initHidden(self):
        return torch.zeros(1, 1, self.gru_size, device=device)
    
    def getEmbedding(self, sentence):
        return F.tanh(self.embedding(sentence))

class LocalAttention(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, dim):
        super(LocalAttention, self).__init__()
        self.W = nn.Linear(dim, dim, bias=False)

    def score(self, decoder_hidden, encoder_out):
        encoder_out = self.W(encoder_out)
        encoder_out = encoder_out.permute(1, 0, 2)
        return encoder_out @ decoder_hidden.permute(1, 2, 0)

    def forward(self, decoder_hidden, encoder_out):
        energies = self.score(decoder_hidden, encoder_out)
        mask = F.softmax(energies, dim=1)
        context = encoder_out.permute(1, 2, 0) @ mask
        context = context.permute(2, 0, 1)
        mask = mask.permute(2, 0, 1)
        return context, mask


class SkipThought(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, vocab_size, embedding_size, gru_size, criterion):
        super(SkipThought, self).__init__()
        self.vocab_size = vocab_size
        self.embedding_size = embedding_size
        self.gru_size = gru_size
        self.criterion = criterion
        
        self.encoder = EncoderRNN(vocab_size, embedding_size, gru_size)
        self.prev_gru = nn.GRU(embedding_size + gru_size, gru_size)
        self.next_gru = nn.GRU(embedding_size + gru_size, gru_size)
        self.attention = LocalAttention(gru_size)
        self.worder = nn.Linear(gru_size * 2, vocab_size)
        self.softmax = nn.LogSoftmax(dim=1)
        
        self.encoder_hidden = self.encoder.initHidden()
    
    def forward(self, input_tensor, prev_tensor, next_tensor, use_teacher_forcing=True):        
        encoder_hidden = self.encoder_hidden
        
        prev_length = prev_tensor.size(0)
        next_length = next_tensor.size(0)
    
        loss = 0
        
        encoder_output, encoder_hidden = self.encoder(input_tensor, encoder_hidden)
    
        prev_input = torch.tensor([[SOS_token]], device=device)
        next_input = torch.tensor([[SOS_token]], device=device)
    
        prev_hidden = encoder_hidden
        next_hidden = encoder_hidden
        
        self.encoder_hidden = encoder_hidden
    
        prev_output = []
        next_output = []
    
        if use_teacher_forcing:
            # Teacher forcing: Feed the target as the next input
            for di in range(prev_length):
                embedded = self.encoder.getEmbedding(prev_input)
                context, _ = self.attention(prev_hidden, encoder_output)
                decoder_output, prev_hidden = self.prev_gru(torch.cat([embedded, context], dim=2), prev_hidden)
                decoder_output = self.softmax(self.worder(torch.cat([decoder_output, context], dim=2)[0]))
                loss += self.criterion(decoder_output, prev_tensor[di])
                prev_output.append( decoder_output.topk(1)[1].squeeze().detach().item() )
                prev_input = prev_tensor[di].unsqueeze(0)  # Teacher forcing
            
            for di in range(next_length):
                embedded = self.encoder.getEmbedding(next_input)
                context, _ = self.attention(next_hidden, encoder_output)
                decoder_output, next_hidden = self.next_gru(torch.cat([embedded, context], dim=2), next_hidden)
                decoder_output = self.softmax(self.worder(torch.cat([decoder_output, context], dim=2)[0]))
                loss += self.criterion(decoder_output, next_tensor[di])
                next_output.append( decoder_output.topk(1)[1].squeeze().detach().item() )
                next_input = next_tensor[di].unsqueeze(0)  # Teacher forcing
    
        else:
            # Without teacher forcing: use its own predictions as the next input
            for di in range(prev_length):
                embedded = self.encoder.getEmbedding(prev_input)
                context, _ = self.attention(prev_hidden, encoder_output)
                decoder_output, prev_hidden = self.prev_gru(torch.cat([embedded, context], dim=2), prev_hidden)
                decoder_output = self.softmax(self.worder(torch.cat([decoder_output, context], dim=2)[0]))
                topv, topi = decoder_output.topk(1)
                prev_input = topi.squeeze().detach()  # detach from history as input
                
                loss += self.criterion(decoder_output, prev_tensor[di])
                prev_output.append( prev_input.item() )
                if prev_input.item() == EOS_token:
                    break
                prev_input = prev_input.unsqueeze(0).unsqueeze(0)
            
            for di in range(next_length):
                embedded = self.encoder.getEmbedding(next_input)
                context, _ = self.attention(next_hidden, encoder_output)
                decoder_output, next_hidden = self.next_gru(torch.cat([embedded, context], dim=2), next_hidden)
                decoder_output = self.softmax(self.worder(torch.cat([decoder_output, context], dim=2)[0]))
                topv, topi = decoder_output.topk(1)
                next_input = topi.squeeze().detach()  # detach from history as input
    
                loss += self.criterion(decoder_output, next_tensor[di])
                next_output.append( next_input.item() )
                if next_input.item() == EOS_token:
                    break
                next_input = next_input.unsqueeze(0).unsqueeze(0)
        
        return loss, prev_output, next_output

Expected behavior
Memory usage in Linux should not linearly increase as the fitting script runs, especially not to the point at which the box dies.

OS (e.g., Linux): Linux (Ubuntu 16.04)

Build command you used (if compiling from source): N/A
Python version: 3.6.6
CUDA/cuDNN version: CUDA 9.0.176 / CuDNN 7.4.1.5
GPU models and configuration: Tesla V100

nodes.bodyText:
🚀 Feature: Support seperated control of the replicating and the collecting of gradients of DataParallel to accelerate it

Add two function to DataParallel, one to replicate models to GPUs, the other to collect gradients.
Motivation
I update the parameters of the designed model after several iterative forward and backward calls, which means that the DataParallel does not need to replicate self.module in every forward call, and it only needs to accumulate the gradients on the other GPUs when I am going to update the parameters with a call to step() of the optimizer. Replicating models in every forward calls greatly hurts the performance in my implementation.

Pitch

I tried to alleviate this through the following code:
class DataParallelModel(DataParallel):
    def __init__(self, module, device_ids=None, output_device=None, dim=0, host_control=False):
        super(DataParallelModel, self).__init__(module, device_ids, output_device, dim)

        if host_control:
	    self.update_replicates()
        else:
	    self.nets = None

    def forward(self, *inputs, **kwargs):
        if not self.device_ids:
            return self.module(*inputs, **kwargs)
        inputs, kwargs = self.scatter(inputs, kwargs, self.device_ids)
        if len(self.device_ids) == 1:
            return self.module(*inputs[0], **kwargs[0])
        if self.nets is None:
            replicas = self.replicate(self.module, self.device_ids[:len(inputs)])
        else:
	    replicas = self.nets[:len(inputs)]
        outputs = self.parallel_apply(replicas, inputs, kwargs)
        return self.gather(outputs, self.output_device)

    def update_replicates(self):
        self.nets = self.replicate(self.module, self.device_ids)

Since I want to make the training more efficient like this:
model = DataParallelModel(designed_model, host_control=True)
crit = get_some_criterion()
optm = get_an_optimizer(model)
update_batches = 16
i = 1
for id, td in training_data():
    loss = crit(model(id), td)
    loss.backward()
    if i % update_batches == 0:
        optm.step()
        model.zero_grad()
        model.update_replicates()
    i += 1

But an assertation failure was thrown by autograd, which is beyond my ability.
I hope it can support another function like accumulate_gradients which accumulates the gradients from those replicated models at the same time, thus I can avoid useless communications between GPUs. In this case, the training code could be like:
model = DataParallelModel(designed_model, host_control=True)
crit = get_some_criterion()
optm = get_an_optimizer(model)
update_batches = 16
i = 1
for id, td in training_data():
    loss = crit(model(id), td)
    loss.backward()
    if i % update_batches == 0:
        model.accumulate_gradients()
        optm.step()
        model.zero_grad()
        model.update_replicates()
    i += 1

Accumulate the gradients of several small batches is very important in some cases where a large batch size is very important for the quality of the model while the GPU memory is not enough to support it, like the training of transformer(a Neural Machine Translation model).
nodes.title: Support the seperated control of the replicating and the collecting of gradients of DataParallel to accelerate it

import torch
import torch.utils.data
import torchvision

class ToCuda:

    def __init__(self):
        self.is_cuda = torch.cuda.is_available()

    def __call__(self, tensor):

transform = torchvision.transforms.Compose([torchvision.transforms.ToTensor(), ToCuda()])
dataset = torchvision.datasets.MNIST('../data', transform=transform)

🐛 Bug

The weight of positive examples should default to 1.. However, there are inputs for which the result is finite without specifying pos_weight and nan with pos_weight=torch.tensor([1.]).
To Reproduce
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
import torch, math 
import torch.nn.functional as F

logits = torch.tensor([0., -120.])
target = torch.tensor([0., 1.])

# passes
assert math.isfinite(
    F.binary_cross_entropy_with_logits(logits, target).item()
)

pos_weight = torch.tensor([1., 1.])

# fails
assert math.isfinite(
    F.binary_cross_entropy_with_logits(logits, target, pos_weight=pos_weight).item()
)
Note that for moderate inputs (-10 instead of -120) this works as expected
Expected behavior
Both cases should lead to the same result, because the latter is just explicitly passing the default value.

Issue description
I have a 80x256x256x10 FC network I'm using for policy gradient, but when I do a forward pass on it it takes 70-100ms (!!) to execute. Puzzling-ly, after some condition that I can't identify, the forward pass suddenly speeds up permanently to < 1-3ms (I couldn't get a reproducible example of that though). Exiting the code during execution seems to imply that it's spending a lot of time in torch.addmm(bias, input, weight.t()). Adding pytorch.set_num_threads(1) seems to fix it, but I don't know why. Sorry if this is a duplicate (I suspect it may be) but I looked and couldn't find anything in the issues
Code example
Here's a (sort of) minimal example that reproduces the slowness:
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F
import numpy as np
import time

class GaussianMLP(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, num_inputs, action_dim, init_std=1, learn_std=True, nonlinearity="tanh"):
        super(GaussianMLP, self).__init__()

        actor_dims = (256, 256)
        critic_dims = (256, 256)

        # create actor network
        self.actor_layers = nn.ModuleList()
        self.actor_layers += [nn.Linear(num_inputs, actor_dims[0])]
        for l in range(len(actor_dims) - 1):
            in_dim = actor_dims[l]
            out_dim = actor_dims[l + 1]
            self.actor_layers += [nn.Linear(in_dim, out_dim)]
        
        self.mean = nn.Linear(actor_dims[-1], action_dim)

        # create critic network
        self.critic_layers = nn.ModuleList()
        self.critic_layers += [nn.Linear(num_inputs, critic_dims[0])]
        for l in range(len(critic_dims) - 1):
            in_dim = critic_dims[l]
            out_dim = critic_dims[l + 1]
            self.critic_layers += [nn.Linear(in_dim, out_dim)]

        self.vf = nn.Linear(critic_dims[-1], 1)

        if nonlinearity == "relu":
            self.nonlinearity = F.relu
        else:
            self.nonlinearity = torch.tanh
        
        self.train()

    def forward(self, inputs):
        start = time.time()
        x = inputs
        for l in self.critic_layers:
            x = self.nonlinearity(l(x))
        value = self.vf(x)

class DotAtt(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self , in_hidden_size = 100 , out_hidden_size = 100):
        super(DotAtt, self).__init__()
        self.in_hidden_size = in_hidden_size
        self.out_hidden_size = out_hidden_size

    def forward(self , qi, c , qi_length , c_length):
        #qi [batch , seq_len , in_hidden]
        #c [batch , con_len , in_hidden]
        #qi_length = [batch]
        #c_length = [batch]
        batch_size , seq_len  = qi.size()[:2]
        con_len = c.size(1)
        mask_qi = torch.ones(batch_size , seq_len)
        mask_c = torch.ones(batch_size , con_len)
        for index , (qi_l , ci_l) in range(zip(qi_length , c_length)):
            mask_qi[index , :qi_l] = 0
            mask_c[index , :ci_l] = 0
        mask_c *= (-1e10)
        mask_qi *= -1e10

        mask_c = mask_c.view(1,batch_size,con_len).repeat(seq_len,1,1)
        mask_qi = mask_qi.view(1,batch_size ,seq_len).repeat(con_len,1,1)


        qi = F.relu(self.W(qi))
        c = F.relu(self.W(c))
        attn = torch.matmul(c ,qi.transpose(-2,-1)) #[batch , con_len , seq_len]
        attn = attn.permute(1,0,2) #[con_len , batch , seq_len]
        attn = attn + mask_qi
        attn = attn.permute(1,0,2).permute(2,0,1) #[seq_len , batch , con_len]
        attn = attn + mask_c
        attn = attn.permute(1,2,0)#[batch , con_len , seq_len]
        attn = F.softmax(attn ,dim = -1)
        qi_hat = torch.matmul(attn , qi) #[batch , con_len , out_hidden]
        return qi_hat

class DotAttHier(nn.Module):

    def forward(self, Q , C , Q_len , C_len):

            # [1 , batch , con_len , out_hidden]

    def forward(self , Q , C , Q_mask , C_mask):
        #Q_len[batch , sess_len]
        batch_size , sess_len , seq_len , in_hidden = Q.size()
        con_len = C.size(1)

        Q = Q.view(batch_size * sess_len , seq_len , in_hidden)
        C = C.repeat(sess_len , 1, 1)
        Q = F.relu(self.W(Q))
        C = F.relu(self.W(C))

        C_mask = C_mask * (-1e10) #[batch , con_len]
        C_mask = C_mask.unsqueeze(-1).repeat(sess_len , 1 , seq_len) #[batch * sess_len , con_len , seq_len]
        attn = attn + C_mask + Q_mask
        attn = F.softmax(attn, dim=-1) #[batch * sess_len , con_len , seq_len(归一化)]

class NaiveLSTM(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self , input_size , hidden_size , batch_first = True,
                 num_layer = 1, num_dir = 2,
                 batch_size = 10 , dropout_p = 0.5,
                 max_length = MAX_LENGTH):
        super(NaiveLSTM,self).__init__()
        self.input_size = input_size
        self.hidden_size = hidden_size
        self.batch_first = batch_first
        self.num_layer = num_layer
        self.num_dir = num_dir
        self.batch_size = batch_size
        self.dropout_p = dropout_p
        self.lstm  = nn.LSTM(
            input_size=input_size,
            hidden_size=hidden_size,
            num_layers=num_layer,
            bidirectional=num_dir > 1,
            batch_first=batch_first,
            dropout=dropout_p
        )

    def forward(self, input , input_length):
        #input = [batch * sess_len , seq_len , hidden_size]
        #input_length = [batch * sess_len]

        sorted_idx = np.argsort(-input_length)
        input = input[sorted_idx]
        input_length = input_length[sorted_idx]

        input = torch.nn.utils.rnn.pack_padded_sequence(input, input_length, batch_first=self.batch_first)
        out, (h_n, c_n) = self.lstm(input=input)
        out, _ = torch.nn.utils.rnn.pad_packed_sequence(out, batch_first=self.batch_first)
        unsorted_idx = np.argsort(sorted_idx)
        out = out[unsorted_idx]  # [batch_size * sess_len, seq_len , num_dir * hidden_size]
        return out

class HierEncoderLSTM(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self ,input_size, hidden_size , batch_first = True,
                 num_layer = 2 , num_dir = 2,
                 batch_size = 10 , dropout_p = 0.5,
                 max_length = MAX_LENGTH):
        super(HierEncoderLSTM,self).__init__()
        self.input_size = input_size
        self.hidden_size = hidden_size
        self.batch_first = batch_first
        self.num_layer = num_layer
        self.num_dir = num_dir
        self.batch_size = batch_size
        self.dropout_p = dropout_p

        self.lstm = nn.LSTM(
            input_size = input_size,
            hidden_size = hidden_size,
            num_layers = num_layer,
            bidirectional= num_dir > 1,
            batch_first = batch_first,
            dropout = dropout_p
        )

        self.w  = nn.Linear(
            num_dir * hidden_size,
            1
        )

        self.high_lstm = nn.LSTM(
            input_size = hidden_size * num_dir,
            hidden_size = hidden_size * num_dir,
            num_layers = 1,
            batch_first = batch_first,
            dropout = dropout_p
        )

    def forward(self , Q , Q_len , Sess_len , Q_mask0):
        batch_size , sess_len , seq_len , input_size = Q.size()
        #Q_len = [batch , sess_len]
        #Q_mask0 = [batch , sess_len , seq_len]
        Q = Q.view(-1 , seq_len , input_size)
        Q_len = Q_len.view(-1)

        sorted_idx = np.argsort(-Q_len)
        out = Q[sorted_idx]
        out_len = Q_len[sorted_idx]

        out = torch.nn.utils.rnn.pack_padded_sequence(out,out_len , batch_first=self.batch_first)
        out, (h_n, c_n) = self.lstm(input=out)
        out, _ = torch.nn.utils.rnn.pad_packed_sequence(out, batch_first=self.batch_first)
        unsorted_idx = np.argsort(sorted_idx)
        out = out[unsorted_idx] #[batch_size * sess_len, seq_len , self.num_dir * self.hidden_size]

        attn = self.w(out) #[batch * sess_len , seq_len , 1]
        Q_mask0 = Q_mask0 * (-1e10)
        Q_mask0 = Q_mask0.view(-1,seq_len).unsqueeze(-1) #[batch * sess_len , seq_len , 1]
        attn = (attn + Q_mask0).transpose(-1,-2) #[batch * sess_len , 1 , seq_len]
        high_out = torch.matmul(attn , out) #[batch * sess_len  , 1 , num_dir * hidden]
        high_out = high_out.squeeze(1).view(batch_size , sess_len , -1)

        sorted_idx = np.argsort(-Sess_len)
        high_out = high_out[sorted_idx]
        Sess_len = Sess_len[sorted_idx]

        high_out = torch.nn.utils.rnn.pack_padded_sequence(high_out , Sess_len, batch_first = self.batch_first)
        high_out , (h_n , c_n) = self.high_lstm(input = high_out)
        high_out , _ = torch.nn.utils.rnn.pad_packed_sequence(high_out , batch_first=self.batch_first)
        unsorted_idx = np.argsort(sorted_idx)
        high_out = high_out[unsorted_idx] #[batch , sess_len , num_dir * hidden]
        return out , high_out

def get_mask(input_length , max_seq_len , mask_value = 0):
    #[batch ] or [batch , sess_len]
    #mask_value = 0 ,有值的地方为0 ，无值的地方为1
    #mask_value = 1 ,有值的地方为1，无值的地方为0
    #for situation 1
    siz = []
    for i in range(len(input_length.size())):
        siz.append(input_length.size(i))
    siz.append(max_seq_len)
    if mask_value == 0:
        mask = torch.zeros(siz).to(device) #[batch, max_seq_len] or[batch , sess_len ,max_seq_len]
    if mask_value == 1:
        mask = torch.ones(siz).to(device)
    input_length = input_length.view(-1) #[batch] or [batch * sess_len]
    mask = mask.view(-1 , max_seq_len)
    for index ,l in enumerate(input_length):
        if mask_value == 0:
            mask[index , l:] = 1
        elif mask_value == 1:
            mask[index , l:] = 0
    mask = mask.view(siz)
    return mask

        super(IF,self).__init__()

        # print("in_hidden_size= ",in_hidden_size)
        # print("hidden_size = ",hidden_size)

        self.in_hidden_size = in_hidden_size
        self.hidden_size = hidden_size
        self.batch_first = batch_first
        self.lstm = nn.LSTM(
            input_size=in_hidden_size,
            hidden_size=hidden_size//2,
            num_layers=num_layer,
            bidirectional=num_dir > 1,
            batch_first=batch_first,
            dropout=dropout_p
        )
        try :
            assert in_hidden_size == hidden_size * 2 + 1
        except:
            print("in_hidden_size = ",in_hidden_size)
            print("hidden_size = ",hidden_size)
            exit(87909)

        self.gru = nn.GRU(
            input_size = hidden_size * num_dir,
            hidden_size = in_hidden_size - hidden_size // 2 * 2,
            batch_first= batch_first,
            dropout= dropout_p,
        )

    def Context_Integration(self , C_h_1 , C_h_len):
        #C_h_1 [batch , sess_len , con_len , in_hidden]
        #C_h_len [batch , sess_len]
        batch_size , sess_len , con_len , in_hidden_size = C_h_1.size()
        C_h_1 = C_h_1.view(-1 , con_len , in_hidden_size)
        C_h_len = C_h_len.view(-1)
        sorted_idx = np.argsort(-C_h_len)
        C_h_1 = C_h_1[sorted_idx]
        C_h_len = C_h_len[sorted_idx]
        print("C_h_len = ",C_h_len)
        C_h_1 = torch.nn.utils.rnn.pack_padded_sequence(C_h_1 , C_h_len , batch_first=self.batch_first)
        C_h_1, (h_n, c_n) = self.lstm(input = C_h_1)
        C_h_1 , _  = torch.nn.utils.rnn.pad_packed_sequence(C_h_1,batch_first=self.batch_first)
        unsorted_idx = np.argsort(sorted_idx)
        C_h_1 = C_h_1[unsorted_idx]
        C_h_1 = C_h_1.view(batch_size,sess_len,con_len,-1)
        return C_h_1

    def Flow(self , C_h , Sess_C_len):
        #Sess_C_len [batch , con_len]
        batch_size , con_len , sess_len , hidden = C_h.size()
        C_h = C_h.view(-1,sess_len,hidden)
        Sess_C_len = Sess_C_len.view(-1)
        sorted_idx = np.argsort(-Sess_C_len)
        C_hat = C_h[sorted_idx]
        Sess_C_len = Sess_C_len[sorted_idx]
        C_hat = torch.nn.utils.rnn.pack_padded_sequence(C_hat, Sess_C_len, batch_first=self.batch_first)
        C_hat , (h_n , c_n) = self.gru(input = C_hat)
        C_hat , _ = torch.nn.utils.rnn.pad_packed_sequence(C_hat , batch_first=self.batch_first)
        unsorted_idx = np.argsort(sorted_idx)
        C_hat = C_hat[unsorted_idx] #[batch * con_len , sess_len , hidden]
        C_h_plus_1 = torch.cat((C_h,C_hat) , dim = -1) #[batch * con_len , sess_len , hidden]
        C_h_plus_1 = C_h_plus_1.view(batch_size , con_len , sess_len , -1).permute(0,2,1,3)
        return C_h_plus_1 #[batch , sess_len , con_len , in_hidden_size]

    def forward(self , C_h_1 , C_h_len , Sess_C_len):
        #C_h_len [batch , sess_len]
        #Sess_C_len [batch , con_len]
        batch_size , sess_len , con_len , in_hidden_size = C_h_1.size()
        # C_h_1 = C_h_1.view( -1, con_len , in_hidden_size)
        C_hat = self.Context_Integration(C_h_1 , C_h_len) #[batch , sess_len , con_len , hidden * 2]
        C_hat = C_hat.permute(0,2,1,3)#[batch , con_len , sess_len , 2 * hidden]
        C_h = self.Flow(C_hat , Sess_C_len) #[batch , sess_len , con_len , hidden * 2 + 1]
        return C_h

class IF3(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self , in_hidden_size , hidden_size ,
                 num_dir =2 , batch_first = True,
                 dropout_p = 0.5 , num_layer = 1):
        super(IF3,self).__init__()
        # print("in_IF3_Class")
        # print("in_hidden_size= ",in_hidden_size)
        # print("hidden_size = ",hidden_size)

        self.in_hidden_size = in_hidden_size
        self.hidden_size = hidden_size
        self.batch_first = batch_first
        self.lstm = nn.LSTM(
            input_size=in_hidden_size,
            hidden_size=hidden_size//2,
            num_layers=num_layer,
            bidirectional=num_dir > 1,
            batch_first=batch_first,
            dropout=dropout_p
        )
        try :
            assert in_hidden_size == hidden_size * 2 + 1 + hidden_size * 2
        except:
            print("in_hidden = ",in_hidden_size)
            print("hidden = ",hidden_size)
            exit(6789)

        self.gru = nn.GRU(
            input_size = hidden_size * num_dir,
            hidden_size = in_hidden_size - hidden_size // 2 * 2,
            batch_first= batch_first,
            dropout= dropout_p,
        )

    def Context_Integration(self , C_h_1 , C_h_len):
        #C_h_1 [batch , sess_len , con_len , in_hidden]
        #C_h_len [batch , sess_len]
        batch_size , sess_len , con_len , in_hidden_size = C_h_1.size()
        C_h_1 = C_h_1.view(-1 , con_len , in_hidden_size)
        C_h_len = C_h_len.view(-1)
        sorted_idx = np.argsort(-C_h_len)
        C_h_1 = C_h_1[sorted_idx]
        C_h_len = C_h_len[sorted_idx]
        C_h_1 = torch.nn.utils.rnn.pack_padded_sequence(C_h_1 , C_h_len , batch_first=self.batch_first)
        C_h_1, (h_n, c_n) = self.lstm(input = C_h_1)
        C_h_1 , _  = torch.nn.utils.rnn.pad_packed_sequence(C_h_1,batch_first=self.batch_first)
        unsorted_idx = np.argsort(sorted_idx)
        C_h_1 = C_h_1[unsorted_idx]
        C_h_1 = C_h_1.view(batch_size,sess_len,con_len,-1)
        return C_h_1

    def Flow(self , C_h , Sess_C_len):
        #Sess_C_len [batch , con_len]
        batch_size , con_len , sess_len , hidden = C_h.size()
        C_h = C_h.view(-1,sess_len,hidden)
        Sess_C_len = Sess_C_len.view(-1)
        sorted_idx = np.argsort(-Sess_C_len)
        C_hat = C_h[sorted_idx]
        Sess_C_len = Sess_C_len[sorted_idx]
        C_hat = torch.nn.utils.rnn.pack_padded_sequence(C_hat, Sess_C_len, batch_first=self.batch_first)
        C_hat , (h_n , c_n) = self.gru(input = C_hat)
        C_hat , _ = torch.nn.utils.rnn.pad_packed_sequence(C_hat , batch_first=self.batch_first)
        unsorted_idx = np.argsort(sorted_idx)
        C_hat = C_hat[unsorted_idx] #[batch * con_len , sess_len ,3 *  hidden + 1]
        C_h_plus_1 = torch.cat((C_h,C_hat) , dim = -1) #[batch * con_len , sess_len ,  4 * hidden + 1]
        C_h_plus_1 = C_h_plus_1.view(batch_size , con_len , sess_len , -1).permute(0,2,1,3)
        return C_h_plus_1 #[batch , sess_len , con_len , in_hidden_size]

    def forward(self , C_h_1 , C_h_len , Sess_C_len):
        #C_h_len [batch , sess_len]
        #Sess_C_len [batch , con_len]
        batch_size , sess_len , con_len , in_hidden_size = C_h_1.size()
        C_h_1 = C_h_1.view( -1, con_len , in_hidden_size)
        C_hat = self.Context_Integration(C_h_1 , C_h_len) #[batch , sess_len , con_len , hidden]
        C_hat = C_hat.permute(0,2,1,3)#[batch , con_len , sess_len , hidden]
        C_h = self.Flow(C_hat , Sess_C_len) #[batch , sess_len , con_len , hidden * 2 + 1]
        return C_h

class FullyAwareAttn(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self , hidden_size , x_hidden_size , y_hidden_size):
        super(FullyAwareAttn , self).__init__()
        self.hidden_size = hidden_size
        self.U_x = nn.Linear(in_features=x_hidden_size,out_features=hidden_size)
        self.U_y = nn.Linear(in_features=y_hidden_size,out_features=hidden_size)
        self.D = torch.diag(torch.rand(hidden_size)) #[hidden,hidden]的对角阵,torch.rand(10),size是10的向量, 【0，1)之间的均匀分布

    def S(self ,C ,Q):
        #C [batch , sess_len , con_len , hidden]
        #Q [batch , sess_len , seq_len , hidden]
        #a[i,j,k] = C[j][i] * Q[j][k] 第j个对话轮次中,C中的第i个单词与Q中的第k个单词计算的相似度
        #a = torch.matmul(C , Q.transpose(-2 , -1)) #[batch , sess_len , con_len , seq_len] 是这个意思，但是不是简单的点乘算相似度
        C = F.relu(self.U_x(C))
        Q = F.relu(self.U_y(Q))
        temp = torch.matmul(C,self.D)
        a = torch.matmul(temp , Q.transpose(-2,-1)) #[batch , sess_len , con_len , seq_len]
        return a

    def forward(self , C , Q , C_mask0 , Q_mask0):
        # C = ( C_zero, C_one, C_two )
        # Q = ( Q_naive , Q_lstm1 , Q_lstm2)
        C_zero, C_one, C_two = C
        embed_Q, Q_lstm_1, Q_lstm_2 = Q
        Q = torch.cat((embed_Q, Q_lstm_1, Q_lstm_2),dim = -1)
        C = torch.cat((C_zero, C_one, C_two), dim=-1)
        batch_size , sess_len , con_len , hidden_size = C.size()
        seq_len = Q.size(2)
        #C_mask0 [batch , con_len]
        #Q_mask0 [batch , sess_len , seq_len]
        a = self.S(C,Q) #[batch , sess_len , con_len , seq_len]
        C_mask0 = C_mask0 * (-1e10)
        Q_mask0 = Q_mask0 * (-1e10)
        C_mask0 = C_mask0.unsqueeze(1).unsqueeze(-1).repeat(1 , sess_len , 1 , seq_len)
        Q_mask0 = Q_mask0.unsqueeze(-2).repeat(1,1,con_len,1)
        a = a + Q_mask0 + C_mask0
        a = F.softmax(a , dim = -1) #[batch , sess_len , con_len , seq_len(归一化)]
        Q_hat = torch.matmul(a , Q_lstm_2) #[batch , sess_len , con_len , hidden]
        return Q_hat

class FlowQA(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self , vocab_size , hidden_size , pad_token_index):
        super(FlowQA,self).__init__()
        self.vocab_size = vocab_size
        self.hidden_size= hidden_size

        self.embedding = nn.Embedding(
            num_embeddings=self.vocab_size,
            embedding_dim=self.hidden_size,
            padding_idx=pad_token_index
        )

        self.dotatthier = DotAttHier2(
            in_hidden_size=hidden_size,
            out_hidden_size = hidden_size
        )

        self.lstm_Q = NaiveLSTM(
            input_size = hidden_size,
            hidden_size = hidden_size,
            num_layer= 1,
            num_dir=2,
            batch_first=True
        )

        self.hierQueEncoder = HierEncoderLSTM(
            input_size = hidden_size,
            hidden_size = hidden_size,
            num_layer=1
        )

        self.IF1 = IF(
            in_hidden_size = 2 * hidden_size + 1,
            hidden_size = hidden_size
        )

        # print("IF1.hidden = ",self.IF1.hidden_size , "IF1.in_hidden = ",self.IF1.in_hidden_size)

        self.IF2 = IF(
            in_hidden_size= 2 * hidden_size + 1,
            hidden_size=hidden_size
        )

        # print("IF2.hidden = ", self.IF2.hidden_size, "IF2.in_hidden = ", self.IF2.in_hidden_size)

        self.FAT_On_Que = FullyAwareAttn(
            hidden_size = hidden_size * 3 ,
            x_hidden_size = (2 * hidden_size + 1) * 3,
            y_hidden_size = (2 * 2 + 1) * hidden_size
        )

        self.IF3 = IF3(
            in_hidden_size= 2 * hidden_size + 1 + 2 * hidden_size,
            hidden_size = hidden_size
        )

        self.FAT_C_self = FullyAwareAttn(
            hidden_size = hidden_size * 3,
            x_hidden_size = (2 * hidden_size + 1) * 3,
            y_hidden_size = (2 * hidden_size + 1) * 3
        )

        self.lstm_C = NaiveLSTM(
            input_size=(2 * hidden_size + 1) * 2,
            hidden_size=hidden_size,
            num_layer=1,
            num_dir=2,
            batch_first=True
        )

        self.predAnsable_W = nn.Bilinear(
            in1_features= 2 * (2 * hidden_size + 1),
            in2_features= 2 * hidden_size,
            out_features= 1
        )

        self.Ws = nn.Bilinear(
            in1_features= 2 * hidden_size + 1,
            in2_features= 2 * hidden_size,
            out_features= 1
        )

        self.ptr_gru = nn.GRUCell(
            input_size= 2 * hidden_size + 1,
            hidden_size = 2 * hidden_size
        )

        self.We = nn.Bilinear(
            in1_features= 2 * hidden_size + 1,
            in2_features= 2 * hidden_size,
            out_features= 1
        )

    def get_common(self, Q , C):
        em = []
        batch_size , sess_len , seq_len = Q.size()
        con_len = C.size(1)
        Q = Q.transpose(0,1) #[sess_len , batch , seq_len]
        for index in range(sess_len):
            temp = []
            for i in range(batch_size):
                tmp = [ 1 if ele in Q[index][i] else 0 for ele in C[i]]
                tmp = FloatTensor(tmp)
                tmp = temp.view(1, -1)
                temp.append(tmp)
            temp = torch.cat(tmp,dim=0)
            temp = temp.view(1,batch_size,con_len)
            em.append(temp)
        em = torch.cat(em,dim=0) #[sess_len ,batch_size , con_len]
        em = em.permute(1,0,2)
        return em

    def get_common2(self, Q ,C):
        em = []
        batch_size, sess_len, seq_len = Q.size()
        con_len = C.size(1)
        Q = Q.transpose(0, 1)  # [sess_len , batch , seq_len]
        for index in range(sess_len):
            temp = [[1 if ele in Q[index][i] else 0 for ele in C[i]] for i in range(batch_size)]
            em.append(FloatTensor(temp).view(1,batch_size,con_len))
        em = torch.cat(em, dim=0) #[sess_len ,batch_size , con_len]
        em = em.permute(1,0,2)
        return em

    def predictAnswerable(self , C_fou , C_mask1 , Q_lstm_high , Sess_len_mask1):
        #C_fou [batch , sess_len , con_len , 2 * hidden + 1]
        #C_mask1 [batch , con_len] 有值的地方为1，无值的地方为0
        #Q_lstm_high [batch , sess_len , 2 * hidden]
        #Sess_len_mask1 [batch , sess_len] 有值的地方为1，无值的地方为0
        batch_size , sess_len , con_len , _ = C_fou.size()
        C_mask1 = C_mask1.unsqueeze(1).unsqueeze(-1).repeat(1,sess_len,1)#[batch , sess_len , con_len , 1]
        C_fou = C_fou * C_mask1

        Sess_len_mask1 = Sess_len_mask1.unsqueeze(-1) #[batch , sess_len , 1]
        Q_lstm_high = Q_lstm_high * Sess_len_mask1

        C_max = C_fou.max(-2)[0] #[batch , sess_len , 2 * hidden + 1]
        C_sum = C_fou.sum(-2) #[batch , sess_len , 2 * hidden + 1]
        C = torch.cat((C_max , C_sum) , dim = -1)  #[batch , sess_len , 2 * (2 * hidden + 1)]

        pred = self.predAnsable_W(C , Q_lstm_high) #[batch , sess_len , 1]
        Sess_len_mask0 = 1 - Sess_len_mask1
        Sess_len_mask0 = Sess_len_mask0 * (-1e10)
        pred = pred + Sess_len_mask0
        pred = pred.view(batch_size , sess_len)
        pred = F.softmax(pred,dim=-1)
        return pred , Sess_len_mask1.squeeze(-1)

    def predictSpan(self , C_fou , C_mask1 , Q_lstm_high , Sess_len_mask1 , max_ans_len = 15):
        # C_fou [batch , sess_len , con_len , 2 * hidden + 1]
        # C_mask1 [batch , con_len] 有值的地方为1，无值的地方为0
        # Q_lstm_high [batch , sess_len , 2 * hidden]
        # Sess_len_mask1 [batch , sess_len] 有值的地方为1，无值的地方为0
        batch_size, sess_len, con_len, _ = C_fou.size()
        C_mask1 = C_mask1.unsqueeze(1).unsqueeze(-1).repeat(1, sess_len, 1)  # [batch , sess_len , con_len , 1]
        C_fou = C_fou * C_mask1

        Sess_len_mask1 = Sess_len_mask1.unsqueeze(-1)  # [batch , sess_len , 1]
        Q_lstm_high = Q_lstm_high * Sess_len_mask1

        Q_lstm_high = Q_lstm_high.unsqueeze(2).repeat(1,1,con_len,1) #[batch , sess_len , con_len , 2 * hidden]
        P_S = self.Ws(C_fou,Q_lstm_high) #[batch , sess_len , con_len , 1]
        P_S = (P_S + (1 - C_mask1) * (-1e10)).squeeze(-1) #[batch , sess_len , con_len]
        P_S = F.softmax(P_S , -1)

        C_fou_i = (C_fou * P_S.unsqueeze(-1)).view(batch_size * sess_len ,con_len , -1).sum(1) #[batch * sess_len , 2 * hidden + 1]
        Q_lstm_high_h_hat = self.ptr_gru(input = C_fou_i , hidden = Q_lstm_high[:,:,0,:].view(batch_size * sess_len , -1))
        #[batch * sess_len , 2 * hidden]
        Q_lstm_high_h_hat = Q_lstm_high_h_hat.view(batch_size , sess_len , -1)

        Q_lstm_high_h_hat = Q_lstm_high_h_hat.unsqueeze(2).repeat(1,1,con_len,1)
        P_E = self.We(C_fou , Q_lstm_high_h_hat) #[batch , sess_len , con_len , 1]
        P_E = P_E + ((1 - C_mask1) * (-1e10)).squeeze(-1) #[batch , sess_len , con_len]
        P_E = F.softmax(P_E , -1)

        return  P_S, P_E , C_mask1.squeeeze(-1)


    def forward(self, Q , C , Q_len , Sess_len , C_len , threadhold = 0.5, max_ans_len = 15):
        #Q [batch , sess_len , seq_len]
        #C [batch , context_len]
        #Q_len [batch , sess_len]
        #Sess_len [batch]
        #C_len [batch]
        embed_Q = self.embedding(Q).to(device=device)
        embed_C = self.embedding(C).to(device=device)
        print("device = ",device)
        batch_size , sess_len , seq_len , in_hidden_size = embed_Q.size()
        con_len = C.size(1)
        Q_mask0 = get_mask(Q_len, seq_len, mask_value=0) #[batch , sess_len ,seq_len]
        C_mask0 = get_mask(C_len, con_len, mask_value=0) #[batch , con_len]
        Q_hat = self.dotatthier(embed_Q,embed_C,Q_mask0,C_mask0)#[batch ,sess_len , con_len , in_hidden]
        em = self.get_common2(Q , C) #[batch , sess_len , con_len]
        em = em.view(batch_size,sess_len,con_len,1)
        C_zero = torch.cat((embed_C.view(batch_size,1,con_len,in_hidden_size).repeat(1,sess_len,1,1), em , Q_hat) , dim = -1)
        #[batch , sess_len , con_len , in_hidden + 1 + in_hidden]
        print("C_zero.shape = ",C_zero.shape)

        C_zero_len = C_len.unsqueeze(1).repeat(1 , sess_len)
        #[batch , sess_len]
        Sess_C_len = Sess_len.unsqueeze(1).repeat(1 , con_len)
        #[batch , con_len]
        C_one = self.IF1(C_zero , C_zero_len , Sess_C_len) ##[batch , sess_len , con_len , hidden * 2 + 1]
        C_two = self.IF2(C_one , C_zero_len , Sess_C_len)

        Q_lstm_1, (h_n, c_n) = self.lstm_Q(input = embed_Q.view(-1 , seq_len ,in_hidden_size) , input_length = Q_len.view(-1))
        #[batch * sess_len , seq_len , num_dir * hidden]
        Q_lstm_1 = Q_lstm_1.view(batch_size , sess_len , seq_len , -1)
        Q_lstm_2 , Q_lstm_high = self.hierQueEncoder(Q = Q_lstm_1 , Q_len = Q_len , Sess_len = Sess_len , Q_mask0 = Q_mask0)
        #[batch , sess_len , seq_len , 2 * hidden]  [batch , sess_len , 2 * hidden]

        Q_attned =  self.FAT_On_Que( (C_zero, C_one, C_two) , (embed_Q, Q_lstm_1, Q_lstm_2) , C_mask0 , Q_mask0)
        # [batch , sess_len , con_len , 2 * hidden]
        temp = torch.cat([C_two , Q_attned] , dim = -1)
        C_thr = self.IF3(temp , C_zero_len , Sess_C_len)
        C_attend =  self.FAT_C_self( (C_one , C_two , C_thr) , (C_one , C_two , C_thr) , C_mask0 , C_mask0)

        C_fou = torch.cat([C_thr , C_attend] , dim = -1) # [batch , sess_len , con_len , 2 * (2 * hidden + 1)]
        C_fou = C_fou.view(batch_size * sess_len , con_len , -1)
        C_fou = self.lstm_C(C_fou, C_zero_len.view(-1))
        C_fou = C_fou.view(batch_size , sess_len , con_len , -1)

        P_answerable , Sess_len_mask1 = self.predictAnswerable( C_fou , (1 - C_mask0) , Q_lstm_high , get_mask(Sess_len , sess_len ,mask_value=1))
        #[batch , sess_len]
        P_answerable_yes_no = P_answerable >= threadhold #不一定要不要注释掉它
        P_start , P_end , P_mask1 = self.predictSpan(C_fou,(1 - C_mask0) , Q_lstm_high , Sess_len_mask1 , max_ans_len)
        #[batch , sess_len , con_len]

        return P_answerable , Sess_len_mask1 , P_start , P_end , P_mask1

def train(model , otherInputs , start_label , end_label , criterion , optimizer):
    #start_label = [batch * sess_len] tensor 类型的

    '''

    # [batch , sess_len]          #[batch , sess_len , con_len]
    loss = 0
    ones = torch.ones(len(start_label))
    batch_size , sess_len , con_len = P_start.size()
    P_start = P_start.view(-1 , con_len)
    P_end = P_end.view(-1,con_len)
    #对于loss有两种操作，1，只选择正确的位置的概率，2，subsample一些错误的位置的概率来进行计算。进行2的时候怎么样保证1中的不被再选中呢 ，  又怎么保证mask的东西不被选中呢。

    #完成1
    start = FloatTensor( [ P_start[i][start_label[i]] for i in range(batch_size * sess_len) ] )
    start_neg = 1 - start
    start = start.view(-1,1)
    start_neg = start_neg.view(-1,1)
    start_p = torch.cat((start_neg , start) , dim = -1)
    loss += criterion(start_p , torch.ones(batch_size * sess_len))

    end = FloatTensor([P_end[i][end_label[i]] for i in range(batch_size * sess_len)])
    end_neg = 1 - end
    end = end.view(-1, 1)
    end_neg = end_neg.view(-1, 1)
    end_p = torch.cat((end_neg, end), dim=-1)
    loss += criterion(end_p, torch.ones(batch_size * sess_len))

    loss.backward()
    optimizer.step()

    return loss.item / batch_size

def reload(args,PATH):
    flowQA_model = FlowQA()
    flowQA_optimizer = optim.Adamax(flowQA_model.parameters(), lr=0.1)
    checkpoint = torch.load(PATH)
    flowQA_model.load_state_dict(checkpoint['model_state_dict'])
    flowQA_optimizer.load_state_dict(checkpoint['optimizer_state_dict'])
    epoch = checkpoint['epoch']
    loss = checkpoint['loss']
    # flowQA_model.eval()
    # flowQA_model.train() 为的是让模型参数可以被训练
    return flowQA_model,flowQA_optimizer

def trainIters(in_file = "/data1/zhengquan/data/CoQA/subTrain_preproed.json", n_epochs = 20,  print_every=1000, plot_every=100, save_every = 100,learning_rate=0.01, batch_size = 2):
    Q, Q_len, A, A_len, C, C_len, Sess_len, start_label, end_label, lang = getData(in_file)
    print("data load finished")
    flowQA_model = FlowQA(vocab_size = lang.n_words , hidden_size = 100, pad_token_index = lang.word2id['<PAD>'] )
    criterion = nn.CrossEntropyLoss(size_average=True, reduce=False)
    flowQA_optimizer = optim.Adamax(flowQA_model.parameters(), lr=0.1)
    '''
    OtherInputs 包括
    Q , C , Q_len , Sess_len , C_len 
    #Q [batch , sess_len , seq_len]
    #C [batch , context_len]
    #Q_len [batch , sess_len]
    #Sess_len [batch]
    #C_len [batch]
    '''
    start = time.time()
    plot_losses = []
    print_loss_total = 0  # Reset every print_every
    plot_loss_total = 0  # Reset every plot_every
    inner_loop_iter = 0
    for iter in range(1, n_epochs + 1):
        '''
        这里的otherInputs和start_label,end_label,才是真正按照batch网里面放的，现在才真的需要在sess_len, seq_len或context_len这个维度上补齐,保证每个batch内的数据格式一致，
        '''
        data = getBatchData((Q, Q_len, A, A_len, C, C_len, Sess_len, start_label, end_label))
        while True:
            temp_data = next(data ,None)
            if temp_data is None:
                break
            #inner_loop_iter += 1
            inner_loop_iter += batch_size
            Q, Q_len, A, A_len, C, C_len, Sess_len, start_label, end_label = temp_data
            OtherInpus = (Q , C , Q_len , Sess_len , C_len)
            loss = train(flowQA_model , OtherInpus , start_label , end_label , criterion , flowQA_optimizer)
            print_loss_total += loss
            plot_loss_total += loss

            if inner_loop_iter % print_every == 0:
                print_loss_avg = print_loss_total / print_every
                print_loss_total = 0
                print('%s (%d %d%%) %.4f' % (timeSince(start, iter / n_epochs),
                                             iter, iter / n_epochs * 100, print_loss_avg))

            if inner_loop_iter % plot_every == 0:
                plot_loss_avg = plot_loss_total / plot_every
                plot_losses.append(plot_loss_avg)
                plot_loss_total = 0

            if inner_loop_iter % save_every == 0:
                temp_num = inner_loop_iter
                path_to_save = os.path.join(DIR_TO_SAVE,"%d"%(temp_num))
                while os.path.exists(path_to_save):
                    temp_num += 1
                    path_to_save = os.path.join(DIR_TO_SAVE, "%d" % (temp_num))
                torch.save({'epoch':iter,
                            'model_state_dict':flowQA_model.state.dict(),
                            'optimizer_state_dict':flowQA_optimizer.state_dict(),
                            'loss':loss}
                           ,path_to_save)

    showPlot(plot_losses)

def evaluate(model , otherInputs , start_label , end_label):
    with torch.no_grad():
        P_answerable, Sess_len_mask1, P_start, P_end, P_mask1 = model(otherInputs)
    return P_start , P_end

if __name__ == "__main__":
    # in_file  = "/data1/zhengquan/data/coqa-train-v1.0.json"
    # Q, Q_len, A, A_len, C, C_len, Sess_len, start_label, end_label, lang = getData(in_file)
    # print(lang.n_words)
    trainIters()

🐛 Bug
I'm not sure if the naming was intentional or not.  But in https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/master/caffe2/python/onnx/backend.py#L910
A function named onnx_graph_to_caffe2_net takes a model, instead of a specific graph.
To Reproduce
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
make call to onnx_graph_to_caffe2_net with the model.graph instead of the model
For example
init_net, predict_net = Caffe2Backend.onnx_graph_to_caffe2_net(onnx_model.graph, device="CPU")
The error you will get is
onnx.onnx_cpp2py_export.checker.ValidationError: The model does not have an ir_version set properly.
As the graph doesn't have a value ir_version, the model does.
The correct behavior would be to call
init_net, predict_net = Caffe2Backend.onnx_graph_to_caffe2_net(onnx_model, device="CPU")
Which works, but the function name may is still misleading.

nodes.bodyText:
🐛 Bug
When using a particular architecture, pytorch is throwing CUDA OOME much faster (with "batch_size" of 10k) than tensorflow (which runs smoothly with "batch_size" of 200k-500k).
To Reproduce
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
I wrote two almost identical implementations of a problematic NN architecture in both pytorch and tensorflow.
Here is PyTorch version:
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

class Model(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, **params):
        super(Model, self).__init__()
        self.windows = [1, 2, 3]

        self.region_emb_layers = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(1, 150,
                                                kernel_size=(window, 300), stride=1) \
                                                for window in self.windows])
        self.beg_conv_layers = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(450, 450, \
                                              kernel_size=(3, 1), stride=1) \
                                              for _ in range(2)])                                   

        self.pooling = nn.MaxPool2d(kernel_size=(3, 1), stride=2)
        self.padding_conv = nn.ZeroPad2d((0, 0, 0, 2))
        self.act_fun = nn.ReLU()
        self.linear_out = nn.Linear(450, 2)

    def forward(self, out, emb):
        outs = [None]*len(self.windows)
        out = emb(out)
        out = out.unsqueeze(1)
        
        for i, (window, region_emb_layer) in enumerate(zip(self.windows, self.region_emb_layers)):
            out_ = region_emb_layer(out)
            out_ = nn.ZeroPad2d((0, 0, 0, window - 1))(out_)
            outs[i] = out_

        out = torch.cat(outs, dim=1)
        
        for beg_conv_layer in self.beg_conv_layers:
            out = self.padding_conv(out)
            out = beg_conv_layer(out)
            out = self.act_fun(out)
            
        out = F.adaptive_max_pool2d(out, (1, 1))
        out = out.view(out.size(0), -1)
        out = self.linear_out(out)
        
        return out

import numpy as np

def gen(dataset_size, batch_size):
    for i in range(dataset_size // batch_size):
        b = np.random.choice([10, 30, 70, 200, 500, 1000])
        a = batch_size // b

        x = np.random.randint(0, 42000, (a, b))
        y = np.random.randint(0, 2, (a,))
        
        yield x, y


device = torch.device('cuda:0')

model = Model().to(device)
model = model.to(device)

print('Model parameters cnt: {}'.format(sum(p.numel() for p in model.parameters())))

emb = nn.Embedding(42000, 300).to(device)
emb.weight.requires_grad_(False)

optimizer = torch.optim.Adam(model.parameters(), lr=1e-3)

dataset_size = int(1e6)
batch_size = 10000

for i, (x, y) in enumerate(gen(dataset_size, batch_size)):
    if i % 10 == 0:
        print(i)

    x = torch.from_numpy(x).to(device)
    y = torch.from_numpy(y).to(device)

    out = model(x, emb=emb)

    crit = nn.CrossEntropyLoss()
    loss = crit(out, y)
    
    optimizer.zero_grad()
    loss.backward()
    optimizer.step()

And tensorflow:
import tensorflow
import numpy as np
import keras
from keras.models import Model
from keras.layers import Lambda, Input, Conv2D, Dense, Flatten, \
Embedding, Concatenate, ZeroPadding2D
from keras.optimizers import Adam
import keras.backend as K


x_in = Input((None,))

x = x_in

x = Embedding(42000, 300, trainable=False)(x)
x = Lambda(lambda x: K.expand_dims(x, axis=3))(x)

x1 = ZeroPadding2D(((0, 2), (0, 0)))(x)
x1 = Conv2D(150, (3, 300), activation='relu')(x1)
x2 = ZeroPadding2D(((0, 1), (0, 0)))(x)
x2 = Conv2D(150, (2, 300), activation='relu')(x2)
x3 = Conv2D(150, (1, 300), activation='relu')(x)

x = Concatenate(axis=3)([x1, x2, x3])

x = Conv2D(450, (3, 1), activation='relu', padding='same')(x)
x = Conv2D(450, (3, 1), activation='relu', padding='same')(x)

x = Lambda(lambda x: K.max(x, axis=1))(x)

x = Flatten()(x)
x = Dense(1, activation='sigmoid')(x)

x_out = x

model = Model(inputs=x_in, outputs=x_out)
opt = Adam(lr=1e-3)
model.compile(loss='binary_crossentropy', optimizer=opt)

print(model.summary())

def gen(batch_size):
  while True:
    b = np.random.choice([10, 30, 70, 200, 500, 1000])
    a = batch_size // b
    x = np.random.randint(0, 42000, (a, b))
    y = np.random.randint(0, 2, (a,))
    
    yield x, y

dataset_size = int(1e6)

model.fit_generator(gen(batch_size), steps_per_epoch=dataset_size//batch_size)

nodes.bodyText:
🐛 Bug
In some situation, JIT gives wrong gradients in backward pass. The following script shows the problem. Note that not only .exp() but also with operators such as .log(), we get the same issue.
To Reproduce
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
import torch
import torch.autograd as autograd

def fn(z):
    return (z.exp() - 0).sum() + (z.exp() - torch.zeros(1000)).sum()

z = torch.tensor(1., requires_grad=True)
fn_jit = torch.jit.trace(fn, (z,))
print(fn(z))
print(fn_jit(z))
print(autograd.grad(fn(z), (z,)))
print(autograd.grad(fn_jit(z), (z,)))

Output:
tensor(2721.0005, grad_fn=<AddBackward0>)
tensor(2721.0005, grad_fn=<AddBackward0>)
(tensor(2721.),)
(tensor(5436.5645),)  # expected 2721

Expected behavior
Gradients of fn and fn_jit should be equal.
Environment

PyTorch Version: nightly build (20181022) using conda
OS: Linux
Python version: 3.6

nodes.bodyText:
🚀 High-level changes:

IMPORTANT: Both Variable and Variable::Impl are removed, and at::Tensor is always the tensor that's passed around in PyTorch, and it can record autograd history when its autograd metadata (AutogradMeta) is not null.
IMPORTANT: Autograd-related function implementations in Variable will be moved to VariableType.
Autograd metadata now lives in an AutogradMeta struct that TensorImpl has a pointer to, and the AutogradMeta is only populated when the at::Tensor requires gradient.
We decide whether to dispatch to VariableType / non-VariableType functions using the at::AutoNonVariableTypeMode in appropriate places internally. (We only dispatch to VariableType functions if we need profiling/JIT-tracing/autograd)
Common Tensor functions (e.g. numel() / sizes() / dim()) are de-virtualized in TensorImpl and have their runtime reduced by 43%-86%.
tensor.is_variable() and options.is_variable() always return true, because every at::Tensor is a variable (and can record autograd history when its AutogradMeta is not null). (We keep options.is_variable(...) for backward compatibility, and raise warning if it's set to false.)
API behavior change: changing shape/storage on tensor.data in Python or tensor.data() in C++ will no longer update tensor.

Pitch
Currently, the distinction between at::Tensor and Variable (subclass of at::Tensor that contains autograd metadata and functions) creates unnecessary cognitive overhead for PyTorch core development. We want to remove this distinction and make it possible to use at::Tensor everywhere in PyTorch. After merging Variable into at::Tensor, here are the common end-user APIs:

When C++ user wants to create a non-history-recording at::Tensor from another at::Tensor:
Current API (unchanged):

auto t = torch::ones({2, 2}, torch::requires_grad()); // t is recording history
auto t_detached = t.detach() // t_detached is the non-history-recording version of t
When the user calls t.detach(), we do the following under the hood:

We do the shallow copy of t's TensorImpl, which copies the storage pointer and all other TensorImpl fields (e.g. size / stride).

Note that subclasses of TensorImpl (e.g. SparseTensorImpl) need to know how to make a shallow copy of themselves, and we dispatch this operation to each TensorImpl subclass' own shallow_copy_and_detach() function (by making the shallow_copy_and_detach() function virtual in TensorImpl and overriding it in TensorImpl subclasses).


We set the AutogradMeta pointer to NULL, to indicate that it doesn't need to record history.
We return an at::Tensor that wraps the new TensorImpl.



When C++ user wants to enable/disable history-recording for an at::Tensor:
Proposed API:

auto t = torch::ones({2, 2});  // t is not recording history (this already works)
t.requires_grad_(true);  // t is recording history now (new API)
t.requires_grad_(false); // t is not recording history anymore (new API)
When the user calls t.requires_grad_(true), we do the following under the hood:

We initialize a struct called AutogradMeta, which stores autograd-specific fields (such as grad_/grad_fn_/grad_accumulator_).
We assign the struct to the AutogradMeta pointer in t's TensorImpl.

When the user calls t.requires_grad_(false), we do the following under the hood:

We set the AutogradMeta pointer in t's TensorImpl to NULL.



When C++ user wants to call non-Variable operations on an at::Tensor when dispatching through type()
Proposed API:

{
  auto t_type = t.type();  // `t_type` is a Variable type if `t` contains AutogradMeta
}
{
  at::AutoNonVariableTypeMode grad_mode(false);  // thread-local guard (new API)
  auto non_var_type = t.type();  // "non_var_type" is a non-Variable type
}
{
  at::AutoNonVariableTypeMode grad_mode(true);  // thread-local guard (new API)
  auto var_type = t.type();  // "var_type" is a Variable type
}
Under the hood, type() checks whether the at::AutoNonVariableTypeMode thread-local guard is enabled when determining the type of the variable.


When C++ user wants to change content of an at::Tensor that has AutogradMeta, without affecting the tensor's grad_fn or version_counter_
Proposed behavior:

auto t = torch::ones({2, 2});
t.requires_grad_(true);
AT_ASSERT(t.current_version() == 0);
t.data().add_(1);  // This is consistent with Python `.data` behavior: changing `.data` of a tensor in Python doesn't affect the tensor's `grad_fn` or `version_counter_`
AT_ASSERT(t.current_version() == 0);
Motivation


Overly Complex OOP design: Currently the distinction between Variable and Tensor is hard to grasp: Variable::Impl is a subclass of TensorImpl, but it also has an at::Tensor data member which internally wraps another TensorImpl. This co-existence of "is-a" and "has-a" relationship makes the code complicated and adds cognitive overhead.  In particular, it's difficult to track which functions we have overridden in Variable::Impl, and which functions are applicable to Tensor vs. Variable (e.g. is_wrapped_number() is only valid on Tensor, not Variable) (for more context, also see note: We regret making Variable hold a Tensor). Ideally, we want to use the same tensor type everywhere in PyTorch code.


Unused data members in Variable::Impl take up cache/memory space: Since Variable::Impl is a subclass of TensorImpl, it contains all of the data members that a normal TensorImpl would have (such as sizes_ / strides_ / etc.). However, the Variable::Impl functions always call into the underlying at::Tensor and ignores the rest of the fields, which causes a lot of wasted cache/memory space.


Virtual functions are slow: We care about how much time it takes to execute common Tensor functions such as numel() / sizes() / dim(). Currently, these functions are virtual in TensorImpl, so that Variable::Impl (a subclass of TensorImpl) can override them and dispatch those calls to the Variable::Impl's underlying at::Tensor. Virtual function calls are slow because they involve an extra vtable lookup. Specifically, we did the following comparison on the most common Tensor functions (all timings are in ns):

Benchmarked commit: f000101
Benchmark script: https://github.com/yf225/benchmark/blob/tensor_functions/timing/cpp2/benchmarks/aten_overheads.cpp
Non-virtual code: master...yf225:nonvirtual_tensorimpl
Virtual code: master...yf225:virtual_tensorimpl

Based on our current implementation, the runtime difference for dim(), numel(), size(), sizes(), and no-op resize() comes from the virtual function call overhead and the at::Tensor data member indirection in Variable::Impl. If we de-virtualize those functions, we would be able to cut the runtime by 43%-86% on the most common Tensor functions.
Breaking changes
Note that this change will break the current API in the following way:
In the old world, whenever we want to create a Variable that shares the same data with another Variable, we simply do auto var_new = make_variable(var.data()) or auto var_new = var.detach(), and any shape / data / storage pointer changes to var_new will be reflected in var automatically, because internally they share the same underlying at::Tensor.
However, in the new world, there is no concept of the "underlying at::Tensor" of a Variable, since the Variable itself is the Tensor. When we want to create an at::Tensor that shares the same data with another at::Tensor, we can still call auto t_new = t.detach(), but in this case, only the tensor storage data is shared (via ref-counted pointer) between t_new and t, but not the tensor size/stride information (they are copied by value). In other words, changing anything (e.g. size / stride / storage_ptr ) in the detached Tensor (t_new) that are not bits inside tensor storage won't update the original Tensor (t), and we should no longer expect those data to be shared.
This has implications for Python call sites that do
tensor.data.in_place_operation_()
or
tensor_detached = tensor.detach()
tensor_detached.in_place_operation_()
If in_place_operation_() only updates the data inside the tensor (such as zeros_()), such operation will still work properly; if the in-place operation changes the size, stride or the storage pointer inside the TensorImpl (e.g. resize_ / resize_as_ / set_ / transpose_), such operation on tensor.data or tensor_detached will no longer update the tensor. We will address this inconsistency in the following ways:

Add an allow_tensor_metadata_change_ flag to TensorImpl to disallow size/stride/storage_ptr changes from in-place operations such as resize_ / resize_as_ / set_ / transpose_, and set this flag to true when people call tensor.data in Python.
Write text in the docs to actively discourage changing the shape or storage of tensor_detached and expecting tensor to also be updated.

Finished changes

 PR: (#13827)


Add a flag to TensorImpl to disallow size/stride/storage_ptr changes from in-place operations such as resize_ / resize_as_ / set_ / transpose_, and set this flag to true when people call tensor.data in Python.
Write text in the docs to actively discourage changing the shape or storage of tensor_detached and expecting tensor to also be updated.
Move Variable::Impl data members into TensorImpl as AutogradMeta struct
Change Variable::Impl functions to use data members in AutogradMeta struct
Add shallow_copy() function to each subclass of TensorImpl
Do shallow copy when the user calls make_variable(tensor) / variable.detach() (Reason: now that autograd metadata lives in TensorImpl, in order to create a new history for for the Variable returned from variable.detach() we not only need to create a new AutogradMeta struct, but we also need to create a new TensorImpl object that stores pointer to the new AutogradMeta struct (which we obtain by shallow-copying the original TensorImpl). Otherwise, changing history of the detached Variable will also change the history of the original Variable, which is not the correct behavior.)
Add AutogradMetaInterface class, and make AutogradMeta a subclass of it, so that we can make autograd_meta_ a unique_ptr in TensorImpl


 PR: (#15487)


Move set_requires_grad() / requires_grad() / grad() from Variable::Impl to AutogradMeta
Move Variable::Impl functions such as backward() / rebase_history() / grad_accumulator() / grad_fn() out of Variable::Impl and into AutogradMeta.
Note: we need to make these changes so that we can remove Variable::Impl class in the next PR.


 PR: (#15939)


Add thread-local guard (at::AutoNonVariableTypeMode) to make sure that in VariableType.cpp the operations on baseType still dispatch to non-Variable type, even if the parameters are now Variables


 PR: (#16305)


Make gesv_out return the original input tensor instead of a new tensor (currently by copying the result tensor into the original input tensor, because a true in-place gesv is more difficult to implement. NOTE: also open an issue for this).
In VariableType.cpp, after each in-place function on the "unpacked" tensor, check pointer address equality for storage in the original input variable's TensorImpl (check this for all arguments in unpacked_args)


 PR: (#16325)


Remove .type() calls as much as possible, to reduce the need of using the at::AutoNonVariableTypeMode guard


 PR: (#16596)


Make JIT attributes t_ and ts_ store Variable instead of Tensor (and in t_ and ts_ use sites, don't wrap the tensor into Variable again) (global search make_variable( in jit/ to find places where we are doing double-wrapping for t_ and ts_ attributes)


 PR: (#17031)


tril_ and triu_ should not change the input tensor's TensorImpl pointer


 PR: (#18225)


Move pyobj_ to TensorImpl itself, because we always need to be able to convert to and from the Python representation.


 PR: (#18223)


Move version_counter_ to storage or TensorImpl, because we may capture non-requires-grad variables inside an autograd function, and we need a working version counter in these cases.
We should not share version counter in shallow_copy_and_detach(), because a pure Tensor doesn't have concept of version counter, and it's managed by autograd instead.
We should preserve the API semantics of tensor.data in Python, and allow it as an escape route for in-place operations without bumping version counter.


 PR: #19139


tensor.is_variable() should check whether the TensorImpl has AutogradMeta. is_variable_ should be removed.



 PR: Fix version counter sharing in Variable.set_data(...) #20391


 PR: Move at::NonVariableTypeMode to TensorImpl, and check it in TensorImpl is_variable() #20392


 PR: Require passing version_counter and allow_tensor_metadata_change to shallow_copy_and_detach(): #20496


 PR: Shallow-copy indices and values in sparse tensor constructor #20330


 PR: Remove Variable::Impl (#17072)



Remove the at::Tensor data member (data_) from Variable::Impl
In Variable construction and in Variable.set_data(), copy all data from data.impl to the variable's TensorImpl.
Make Variable.data() the same semantics as tensor.data in Python. Notice breakage in any Variable.data() call sites
Remove the Variable::Impl class and the DifferentiableViewImpl class
Remove mentions of Variable::Impl and DifferentiableViewImpl
Fix comments in [Tensor versus Variable in C++], [We regret making Variable hold a Tensor], [ Autograd View Variables ]. Go through all comments in variable.h and variable.cpp and fix any inconsistency.
NOTE: we don't need to add SparseVariableImpl that handles how to copy SparseTensorImpl, because SparseTensorImpl already implements the shallow_copy_and_detach() function that Variable factory functions can call.
In places where we need to ensure the tensor is not requiring gradient, we should check !requires_grad() || at::NonVariableTypeMode::is_enabled(), instead of !requires_grad() || !at::GradMode::is_enabled(), because we don't want to move at::GradMode to ATen.

Changes remaining:


 Make AutogradMeta optional, so that Variable and Tensor become the same. (Tracking issue: #23032)


 Miscellaneous cleanup



Remove unpack() in VariableType*.cpp.
Clean up the unpack_args logic in gen_variable_type.py, since we are not doing unpack anymore.
Fix comments for use_derived in gen_variable_type.py
Remove requires_tensor: True in native_functions.yaml. Figure out how to fix _dimV, _dimS case (torch.randn(2, 3)._dimV() shouldn't hit that error)



 TensorImpl de-virtualization (tracking issue: #22815)


 Sparse invariant fix (tracking issue: #22778)


 Remove tensor_data() API (@yf225 is working on it)


 Python / C++ Tensor API parity (@yf225 is working on it)



Any Python Tensor API should also work on C++ Tensor, without explicit casting to Variable


 C++ API doc fix: (@yf225 is working on it)


Remove https://pytorch.org/cppdocs/#aten section, and replace all at::Tensor with torch::Tensor, and remove/fix all mentions of ATen in cpp docs and tutorials.
